implementationStatus: The file-backed text audit operation is implemented by W12-S02 and the streaming raw-byte occurrence source with bounded same-read windows is implemented by W13-S03; the remaining proposed source shapes are not implied to be installed by this document.
principles: A source method names its relational unit; SQL projection never changes that unit.
Occurrence, matching-line, matching-file, count, path, byte-occurrence and coordinated-pattern rows are different units.
A zero-match answer is not a completed scan record; audit carries terminal execution facts.
The audit method starts a new scan for every invocation and never reads global last-run state.
Pattern labels are part of the row identity for many; equal pattern text under different IDs is not deduplicated.
All byte coordinates are offsets and lengths in original input bytes; UTF-16 coordinates use explicitly different names.

callShapes.name: matches
callShapes.cardinality: one row per (Path, PatternId, MatchIndex); PatternId is null for the single-pattern form

callShapes.name: lines
callShapes.unit: one physical line containing one or more occurrences of one pattern
callShapes.cardinality: one row per (Path, PatternId, LineNumber); multiple occurrences on a line remain one row

callShapes.name: files
callShapes.unit: one file satisfying the positive match
callShapes.cardinality: one row per matching (Path, PatternId); a file is emitted once after its first qualifying occurrence

callShapes.name: counts
callShapes.cardinality: one row per eligible Path, including files with zero occurrences

callShapes.name: paths
callShapes.cardinality: one row per eligible Path; this method does not inspect file content

callShapes.name: many
callShapes.unit: one occurrence of one labeled pattern
callShapes.cardinality: one row per (Path, PatternId, MatchIndex); equal pattern text under distinct IDs produces distinct rows

callShapes.name: bytes
callShapes.unit: one occurrence of a byte pattern
callShapes.cardinality: one row per (Path, PatternId, MatchIndex); overlapping policy is fixed by the match-semantics contract
